Psalms 1:1

Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, and did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit in the seat of pestilent men;

  1. Psalms 25:4-5 Refusal of the company of evildoers

    The blessed person refuses the counsel, way and seat of the ungodly. Psalm 25 likewise refuses to sit with an empty council or the ungodly and rejects an assembly of evildoers; the shared concern is chosen association with wrongdoing.

    Read matching passage

    Psalms 25:4 I did not sit with a council of emptiness, and I will certainly not enter with transgressors.

    Psalms 25:5 I hated an assembly of evildoers, and I will certainly not sit with the ungodly.

    Pinned source record

Psalms 1:2

but his will is in the Lord’s law, and on His law he will meditate day and night.

  1. Joshua 1:8 Meditation on the law day and night

    Both texts describe meditation on the law day and night. Joshua connects this discipline with doing what is written and prospering, while the psalm says the blessed person's will is in the Lord's law.

    Read matching passage

    Joshua 1:8 This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth. Meditate on it day and night, so that you may understand how to do all that is written. Then you shall prosper and make your ways prosper, and then you shall understand.

    Pinned source record

Psalms 1:3

He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and whose leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.

  1. Jeremiah 17:7-8 Watered tree and continuing fruitfulness

    The psalm compares the blessed person to a tree beside waters, bearing seasonal fruit without losing its leaf. Jeremiah compares the person trusting the Lord to a tree beside waters that continues bearing fruit through heat and drought.

    Read matching passage

    Jeremiah 17:7 And blessed is the person who has trusted in the Lord, and the Lord will be his hope;

    Jeremiah 17:8 and he will be like a tree flourishing beside waters, and will send its roots toward moisture, and will not fear when heat comes. Wooded stems will be upon it; in a rainless year it will not fear or cease bearing fruit.

    Pinned source record

Psalms 1:4

Not so the ungodly, not so, but like chaff which the wind flings away from the face of the earth.

  1. Job 21:18 Wind-scattered plant matter and the wicked

    The psalm pictures the ungodly as chaff flung away by wind. In Job's discussion of the wicked, they are compared with straw before wind and dust swept by a storm; the shared image is instability and dispersal, within different arguments about their fate.

    Read matching passage

    Job 21:18 They will be like straw before the wind, or like dust that a storm swept away.

    Pinned source record

Psalms 1:5

Therefore the ungodly will not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the council of the righteous;

  1. Matthew 13:49-50 Exclusion of the evil from the righteous in judgment

    The psalm says the ungodly will not rise in judgment and excludes sinners from the righteous council. Jesus' explanation of the net separates the evil from the righteous at the age's consummation. This compares exclusion from the righteous company without turning the psalm's wording into a separate claim about resurrection.

    Read matching passage

    Matthew 13:49 So it will be at the consummation of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from the midst of the righteous

    Matthew 13:50 and cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

    Pinned source record

for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the ungodly will perish.

  1. Psalms 36:18-20 Known righteous ways and the perishing of sinners

    Psalm 1 contrasts the Lord's knowledge of the righteous way with the perishing of the ungodly way. Psalm 36 says the Lord knows the ways of the blameless and contrasts their enduring inheritance with sinners who perish.

    Psalms 36:18 The Lord knows the ways of the blameless, and their inheritance will last for ever.

    Psalms 36:19 They will not be put to shame in an evil time, and in days of famine they will be filled.

    Psalms 36:20 For sinners will perish; the Lord’s enemies, as soon as they are glorified and exalted, vanished away like smoke—they vanished.

Psalms 2:6

“But I was appointed king by Him on Zion, His holy mountain,

  1. 2 Samuel 5:7-12 Zion and kingship established by the Lord

    2 Samuel 5:10 David grew greater and greater, and the Lord Almighty was with him.

    2 Samuel 5:11 Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, cedar wood, woodworkers, and stoneworkers. They built a house for David.

Psalms 2:7

announcing the Lord’s decree: The Lord said to me, ‘You are My son; today I have begotten you.

  1. Acts 13:32-33 Explicit citation of the second psalm

    Acts explicitly names the second psalm and quotes the decree about the Son begotten today in its announcement that God fulfilled the fathers' promise by raising Jesus. The reference and its application are stated in the target itself.

    Read matching passage

    Acts 13:32 We proclaim to you the good news of the promise made to the fathers:

    Acts 13:33 God has fulfilled this for us, their children, by raising up Jesus, as it is also written in the second psalm: ‘Thou art My Son; today I have begotten Thee.’

    Pinned source record

  2. Hebrews 1:5 Sonship decree in the comparison with angels

    Hebrews quotes the Lord's declaration of sonship and begetting today while asking which angel ever received such speech. The royal decree is used in the target's argument concerning the Son's distinction from angels.

    Read matching passage

    Hebrews 1:5 For to which of the angels did He ever say, “Thou art My Son; today I have begotten Thee”? And again, “I will be a Father to Him, and He will be a Son to Me”?

    Pinned source record

    Hebrews quotes the decree about sonship and begetting today when explaining that Christ did not glorify Himself to become high priest. Its context joins the quoted declaration to divine calling, rather than self-assumed honor.

    Read matching passage

    Hebrews 5:5 So also Christ did not glorify Himself to become high priest, but the One who said to Him, “Thou art My Son; today I have begotten Thee,”

Psalms 2:8

Ask of Me, and I will give you nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession.

  1. Daniel 7:14 Granted authority over nations

    The son is promised nations as an inheritance and the earth's ends as a possession. Daniel's vision describes authority given to the figure of the preceding verse and worship by all the earth's nations. Both portray worldwide dominion as granted, without forcing the two passages' figures into an independently established identity.

    Read matching passage

    Daniel 7:14 Authority was given him, and all the nations of the earth according to their families, and all glory, worshipped him. His authority is everlasting authority that will never be taken away, and his kingdom will never be destroyed.

Psalms 2:9

You will shepherd them with an iron rod; you will crush them like a potter’s vessel.’”

  1. Isaiah 30:14 Judgment as the shattering of pottery

    The nations are to be crushed like a potter's vessel. Isaiah compares the coming collapse to an earthen vessel shattered beyond useful fragments. The particular comparison is the destructive pottery image; Isaiah's warning concerns its own disobedient audience.

    Read matching passage

    Isaiah 30:14 and its fall will be like the shattering of an earthen vessel, fine pieces from a jar, so that no shard is found among them with which to lift fire or draw a little water.”

And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all who judge the earth.

    Wisdom of Solomon 6:3 for your rule was given you by the Lord, and your authority by the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your plans.

Psalms 3:1

A psalm of David, when he was fleeing from the presence of Absalom his son.

  1. 2 Samuel 15:13-16 Named historical setting of flight from Absalom

    The title places David's psalm during flight from his son Absalom. The narrative reports Israel's support for Absalom and David's command to flee Jerusalem, followed by his departure with his household; it directly supplies the setting named by the title.

    Read matching passage

    2 Samuel 15:14 David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, “Rise, let us flee, for we have no deliverance from Absalom. Hurry to leave, lest he hurry and overtake us, thrust calamity upon us, and strike the city with the sword’s edge.”

    2 Samuel 15:15 The king’s servants said to the king, “Whatever our lord the king chooses—here are your servants.”

    2 Samuel 15:16 The king went out, with all his household on foot. The king left ten of his concubines to guard the house.

    2 Samuel 15:13 A messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom.”

Psalms 3:3

Many say to my soul, “There is no salvation for him in his God.” Diapsalma.

  1. 2 Samuel 16:7-12 Hostile interpretation of David's calamity

    The psalm reports claims that God offers the speaker no salvation. During David's flight, Shimei interprets his calamity and the transfer of the kingdom to Absalom as the Lord's repayment, while David still hopes for the Lord's favor. This compares the hostile theological accusation without identifying the psalm's many speakers solely with Shimei.

    Read matching passage

    2 Samuel 16:7 Shimei said as he cursed, “Get out, get out, man of bloodshed, lawless man!

    2 Samuel 16:8 The Lord has brought back upon you all the blood of Saul’s house, because you became king in his place. The Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. Now you are in calamity, because you are a man of bloodshed.”

    2 Samuel 16:9 Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? I will cross over and take off his head.”

    2 Samuel 16:10 The king said, “What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Leave him alone, and let him curse this way, because the Lord has told him to curse David. Who can say, ‘Why have you done this?’”

    2 Samuel 16:11 David said to Abishai and all his servants, “My own son, who came from my belly, seeks my life. And now this son of the Benjaminite as well! Leave him alone to curse, for the Lord has told him.

    2 Samuel 16:12 Perhaps the Lord will look upon my humiliation and repay me with good things in place of his curse this day.”

    Pinned source record
